title: Starry Bridge implementation ignition huddle
summary: Kickoff for Starry Bridge onboarding to Redwood inference platform. Focus: staging connectivity, deployment mode decision (Dedicated vs Private), security checklist (KMS/SAML/SOC2), and pilot scope (latency benchmarks, token cost targets). Agreement on 2-week pilot window and next deliverables: runbook, security pack, pricing sheet, benchmark plan.
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-10-13 15:00 UTC | Duration: 47m
Attendees: Maya, Daniel, Sofia, Tom (Redwood) — Olivia, Marcus, Priya, Ben (Starry Bridge)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining — quick roll call, we're Maya from Redwood AE, Daniel our solutions engineer, Sofia CSM. you good to go?
[00:18] Olivia: yep Olivia here, Marcus, Priya and Ben on my side. thanks for the time.
[00:25] Maya: awesome. objective for today is to align staging connectivity, pick a deployment path, and line up the pilot metrics. should be about 45 minutes.
[00:40] Daniel: quick context — Starry Bridge had mentioned you currently run an open model self-hosted stack behind k8s, can you confirm?
[00:49] Ben: yeah we run modified llama variants, k8s on aws, terraform, some custom quantization. latency's ok until load spikes then it goes weird — p95 spikes.
[01:06] Marcus: and cost is creeping up; with our caching we still see waste on cold starts.
[01:14] Daniel: thanks. so two big themes — reliability (latency SLOs) and unit cost. Redwood can help with dedicated capacity or private vpc; we also have hosted for fast time to value.
[01:30] Olivia: prefer private vpc because of compliance, also EU data residency concerns — a lot of users are EU-based.
[01:40] Priya: security is primary — SOC2, SAML SSO, KMS/HSM integration. audit logs are a must.
[01:50] Maya: totally. we'll go through our private deployment options and the controls we support. Daniel, can you walk through the runtime differences quickly?
[02:02] Daniel: sure. the runtime is GPU optimized — continuous batching, kv cache, kernel selection depending on model. when you hit high concurrency we do adaptive batching to keep latency under control. caveat: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools while Private hosts the control plane in your VPC — on-prem air gap is also an option though that one has longer lead times.
[02:30] Ben: when you say kv cache is that per-instance? we've got an architecture that shards kv across nodes and sometimes the cache TTLs cause incoherence.
[02:42] Daniel: good question — we can enable shared prefix/kvcache at the routing layer for some patterns; there's also local KV for very low latency per worker. we'll need to map to your access patterns in the pilot.
[02:56] Marcus: what's the expected p50/p95 numbers for a typical LLM workload? we've seen p50 around 140-180ms in a tuned setup.
[03:07] Tom: in our hosted benchmarks we routinely hit p50 < 120ms for 1k token generation with the usual LLaMA-like backends; p95 depends on batching and concurrency but with Dedicated you can get much tighter tail latency. we'll include bench numbers for your target tokens.
[03:24] Priya: encryption at rest — does Redwood integrate with our AWS KMS? and HSM for keys?
[03:32] Sofia: yes, Private supports customer-managed KMS, and for Dedicated we also offer KMS integration; HSM-based signing is part of the enterprise package. we'll share the security pack.
[03:46] Olivia: what about audit logs and retention? legal wants 1 year of request metadata.
[03:53] Maya: we have configurable retention on audit logs; longer retention is an add-on. also token-level cost breakdowns and per-route dashboards in the console.
[04:06] Ben: can we see traces mapped to user requests? we have tracing using jaeger.
[04:12] Daniel: yes, we have tracing hooks and you can export to your existing observability — jaeger, datadog, prometheus. mapping token spans to user requests requires instrumentation on your side but we emit the traces.
[04:29] Marcus: timeline — we are hoping to start pilot in 2 weeks and go to prod in 8-10 weeks if pilot goes well. is that realistic?
[04:37] Maya: pilot in 2 weeks is tight but doable for a staging run if we have quick network access and creds. production timeline depends on Dedicated capacity procurement if you go that route.
[04:48] Priya: procurement will want SOC2 documentation and a data processing agreement before any prod rollout.
[04:55] Sofia: we'll attach our SOC2 package, DPIA, and DPAs to the follow-up email.
[05:03] Olivia: sounds good. let's talk pilot scope — what should we include?
[05:08] Daniel: minimal pilot: wire up staging VPC peering, run a baseline bench with your prompts, validate token-level cost and p50/p95 across a 1k concurrent user pattern, run failover tests (fallback to smaller model), and validate observability.
[05:26] Ben: can we do a cross-region test — EU and US?
[05:30] Tom: yes, we can route requests by region. private VPC in eu-west is available in our private offering; for Dedicated, we can provision region-specific capacity.
[05:42] Marcus: how much time to provision Dedicated GPUs for our initial commit?
[05:46] Maya: typically 2-4 weeks for capacity allocation depending on commit size; we can do a burst/bridge to Hosted while capacity is locked-in.
[05:56] Olivia: cost — can you ballpark unit cost improvement vs our current infra?
[06:03] Tom: depends on utilization; on average customers see 20-40% reduction after enabling batching and cache profiles; quantization can further reduce cost, but model quality tradeoffs need to be evaluated.
[06:18] Ben: we've already applied int8 quant but have seen hallucination increase for some prompts.
[06:24] Daniel: that's expected; part of Redwood Optimize is to suggest quantization profiles per workload. we'll run a quality guardrail set in pilot to measure regressions.
[06:38] Priya: SSO — SAML or OIDC? we use SAML currently integrated to Okta.
[06:44] Sofia: we support SAML SSO + SCIM for provisioning; RBAC roles available in the console.
[06:51] Marcus: any blockers around VPC peering? we use strict egress rules and private subnets.
[06:57] Daniel: we do require specific firewall rules and a NAT for control-plane handshake; for fully air-gapped on-prem we need a different plan. we'll send the network checklist.
[07:09] Olivia: great. I'd like to see a proposed success criteria list — p50 < 200ms, p95 < 500ms, token cost per 1M under $X, no P1 incidents in 2-week pilot.
[07:21] Maya: noted. we'll put those in the runbook and quantify cost.
[07:27] Ben: do you have prebuilt terraform modules or IaC to add to our infra repo?
[07:33] Tom: yes, we have terraform modules for peering, roles, and runtime config. we'll share the repo links.
[07:40] Priya: security review — do you support certificate rotation and key rotation policies?
[07:45] Sofia: yes, certificate rotation and KMS key rotation policies supported. we'll include rotation docs and the SOC2 control mapping.
[07:55] Marcus: curious if Redwood has experienced regressions when enabling aggressive batching — any notes on user-visible latency spikes?
[08:03] Daniel: batching introduces microqueueing; we do adaptive batching to reduce impact, and we can tune thresholds per route. the console includes previews for batching impact. ocasional mis-queueing happened in an older kernel; fixed in recent runtime patch.
[08:22] Olivia: any competitors we should consider? we're looking at Managed offerings from one of the big clouds and also a smaller inference vendor.
[08:29] Maya: sure — common ones are cloud-provider managed endpoints and some inference-only providers; we can outline pros/cons.
[08:36] Marcus: ok. next let's map the exact network steps so we can hit pilot in 2 weeks.
[08:42] Tom: step 1: share network checklist (we will). step 2: create staging creds, you'll provide vpc peering info. step 3: run bench with our se script. step 4: security review parallel.
[09:00] Ben: bench scripts — are they open? can we run them in our env?
[09:04] Daniel: yes, we'll give you the bench harness, and you can run both client-side and we can run against Redwood to compare.
[09:12] Priya: any E2E encryption in transit specifics? we need mTLS.
[09:17] Sofia: mTLS is supported for Private; we'll include the cert config.
[09:24] Olivia: what's the rollback story if a new model rollout causes quality regression?
[09:29] Tom: the platform supports canary rollouts and automatic fallback policy; you can pin versions and policy will fallback to previous model if quality/regression thresholds are hit.
[09:40] Marcus: who will own the pilot on Redwood side?
[09:43] Maya: I'll be AE point, Daniel and Tom will run the bench and infra, Sofia the success metrics and security pack.
[09:52] Priya: and on our side I'll own security validation, Marcus infra, Ben will run bench and ML quality checks.
[09:59] Maya: great. any immediate red flags?
[10:02] Olivia: nothing blocking, maybe timeline if SOC2 docs take long.
[10:08] Maya: we'll try to get docs in 24-48 hours.
[10:12] Daniel: small note — sometimes auto-transcripts confuse product names, e.g., "KV cache" may show as "K V cash" in transcription exports — noted.
[10:23] (laughter)
[10:27] Maya: ok let's enumerate action items and next steps.
[10:31] [10:31] ACTIONS / NEXT STEPS
[10:33] Maya: 1) Redwood to send security pack + SOC2 evidence (Sofia) — target 2025-10-15.
[10:41] Sofia: yes.
[10:42] Daniel: 2) Redwood to share network checklist and terraform modules (Tom) — target 2025-10-14.
[10:49] Tom: I'll upload links.
[10:50] Ben: 3) Starry Bridge to provide staging VPC peering details and Okta SAML metadata (Olivia/Priya) — target 2025-10-14.
[10:59] Marcus: 4) Run bench: Redwood to provide bench harness and run sample tests; Starry Bridge to run client-side bench same week (joint).
[11:08] Maya: 5) Redwood to send pricing sheet and pilot scope doc (Maya) — target 2025-10-15.
[11:16] Olivia: agreed.
[11:18] Daniel: we'll schedule a bench kick-off call for 2025-10-16 tentatively.
[11:24] Maya: anything else?
[11:27] Priya: one more question about data residency — do you support EU-only control plane?
[11:33] Sofia: Private deployments can have control plane in your region; we'll note region-specific options in the security pack.
[11:42] Olivia: that's it from me. thanks everyone.
[11:45] Maya: recap: send security docs, network checklist, terraform modules, bench harness, pricing. pilot in two weeks pending peering and docs. we'll follow up with calendar invites.
[11:58] Meeting ends
